Internal FCA driver

Source: R/04-compute_fca.R
compute_fca.Rd

Checks the grids, binds the supply to the facility IDs, runs the two-pass block engine and returns a SpatRaster on the grid of the first raster of `rasters`. That raster also names the facilities; the wrappers pass the distance raster first.

Usage

compute_fca(
  demand,
  supply,
  rasters,
  kernels,
  demand_normalize = "identity",
  id_col = NULL,
  supply_cols = NULL,
  indicator_names = NULL,
  snap = FALSE
)

Arguments

demand

One-layer SpatRaster of demand, or a named list of them (one per demand group).

supply

Vector, matrix or data frame, as for [compute_access()].

rasters

Named list of the other SpatRasters the kernels read; the first one has one layer per facility. A key must not name two different rasters.

kernels

`list(demand = function(b, rows), access = function(b, rows))` as for `.fca_blocks()`, or a list of them over the groups.

demand_normalize

Normalization of the demand kernel.

id_col

Character; column name for facility IDs if supply is a data.frame

supply_cols

Character vector; names of supply columns if supply is a data.frame

indicator_names

Character vector; custom names for output accessibility layers

snap

Logical; if TRUE enable fast computation mode (default = FALSE)

Value

SpatRaster of accessibility.

Details

Ungrouped, `demand` is one SpatRaster, `kernels` one kernel pair and the result has one layer per supply measure. Grouped, `demand` is a named list of one-layer SpatRasters (the names are the group IDs), `kernels` a list over the groups, named by group ID, of such pairs, and `rasters` holds the rasters the kernels read, every key ending in `.<group>` (see `.fca_decay_spec()`). The result then has the layers `<measure>.<group>` and `<measure>.all` (see `.fca_blocks()` and `.fca_layer_table()`), and a `layers` attribute: the layer table, a data frame with the columns `layer`, `measure` and `group` (`"all"` for the overall layer). The attribute is read by the wrapper right away, which stores it in `parameters$layers`; it does not survive raster arithmetic.
